title: Aamir Khan Is Married. The First Photo Is Everything.
excerpt: The superstar wed Gauri Spratt in a rain-soaked Mumbai ceremony today — their sons by their side, 150 guests, and a love story 25 years in the making.
body:
It rained all weekend in Mumbai. The kind of monsoon downpour that shuts down highways, floods local trains, and makes you cancel every plan you've ever had. Workers at **Aamir Khan's** Pali Hill bungalow in Bandra wore raincoats while stringing up the last of the floral decorations on Saturday night.

None of it mattered. On Sunday morning, July 5, Aamir Khan married **Gauri Spratt** anyway.

The first photograph from inside the ceremony is the kind of image that stays with you. The superstar sits at a rustic wooden table, dressed in an understated off-white kurta, pen in hand, signing the marriage registry under the Special Marriage Act. Next to him, Gauri — in an elegant ivory ensemble with intricate embroidery, a statement necklace, minimal makeup — looks exactly like someone who knows this is the most important document she'll ever witness.

But the detail that makes the photo extraordinary is between them. Gauri's young son, **Quinn**, stands right there, leaning over the table, peering at the papers with the intense curiosity of a seven-year-old watching his world rearrange itself. On Aamir's other side, his youngest son **Azad Rao Khan** — the child he shares with filmmaker **Kiran Rao** — sits in a peach-coloured kurta, watching his father begin again.

Two children. Two families. One table.

## The Ceremony

The wedding was exactly what Aamir promised it would be: small, warm, and deeply personal. Around 100 to 150 guests — close family, childhood friends, and a tight circle of industry colleagues — gathered at the actor's residence, which had been transformed with soft pastel florals and candlelight into something that looked less like a Bollywood wedding and more like a Tuscan garden party.

Filmmaker **Ashutosh Gowariker** — Aamir's collaborator on *Lagaan*, which is celebrating its 25th anniversary this year — was spotted among the guests. Some family members were flown in from overseas. There was no red carpet. No paparazzi inside the gates. No grand Bollywood reception planned.

> "Bahut hi chhoti si shaadi hai. Ghar par hi kar rahe hain, dono families ke saath." — Aamir Khan, confirming the wedding to the press

## A Love Story That Took 25 Years

Aamir and Gauri's story is the kind of thing a screenwriter would reject for being too on-the-nose. They first met nearly 25 years ago — in a different era of Bollywood, a different era of their lives — and then lost touch completely. They reconnected in 2024 through Aamir's cousin, **Nuzhat Khan**, in Bengaluru, where Gauri was living.

What followed was a long-distance relationship that gradually became something more. In March 2025, during his 60th birthday celebrations, Aamir introduced Gauri to the media as his partner — a move that was both vulnerable and characteristically deliberate. He later revealed he had personally introduced her to both **Shah Rukh Khan** and **Salman Khan**, his two closest friends in the industry.

Gauri herself is no ordinary partner. Born in Bengaluru, she studied fashion design and photography in London. Her grandfather, **Philip Spratt**, was a British-born Communist who sailed to India in the 1920s and became deeply involved in the country's freedom movement — a lineage that bridges continents and centuries. She has been associated with Aamir Khan Productions since relocating to Mumbai.

This is Aamir's third marriage. His first, to **Reena Dutta** (with whom he has children **Junaid** and **Ira**), ended after 16 years. His second, to filmmaker **Kiran Rao**, ended in 2021 with a joint statement so graceful it became a template for how public separations can be handled with dignity.

## For the Diaspora

Aamir Khan occupies a singular space in the hearts of the Indian diaspora. He's the man who made *Lagaan* — a film that got nominated for an Oscar and made NRIs feel, maybe for the first time, that Bollywood could stand on the world stage. He's the man behind *3 Idiots*, which became a cultural shorthand for every diaspora kid pushed into engineering. He's the man who made *Dangal*, which grossed over ₹2,000 crore worldwide and turned an Indian wrestling story into China's favourite Bollywood film.

So when he signs a piece of paper in the rain, it feels like news. Not because of gossip or scandal — but because for millions of Indians scattered across the world, Aamir Khan's happiness feels personal.

The monsoon is still hammering Mumbai tonight. Inside a house in Pali Hill, they're probably still celebrating.

Congratulations, Mr. and Mrs. Khan.
